A1.justification: Both PDFs are identifiable revisions of Splits!, retaining the authors, Reddit source corpus, six demographics and much of the dataset construction. All pages, including appendices, are readable. The substantial changes in research focus and evaluation can be reliably compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM benchmarking, human ratings, calibration and classifier experiments, and demographic/topic results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 reports original corpus analyses replicating linguistic phenomena, generated-hypothesis evaluations, and human validation of Triviality in Sections 3–6 and Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: v1 generates natural-language theories from unlabeled calibration posts and evaluates them through a fixed Llama demographic classifier. v2 replaces this with lexical hypotheses evaluated through BM25 reranking, lift and BERT-based subspace Triviality. Dataset topic selection also changes from BM25 filtering to ColBERT retrieval with an LLM-guided cutoff algorithm.

E1.justification: The six demographics and 2012–2018 Reddit source remain, but the evaluated task shifts from neutral-topic Group Theorization and demographic attribution to lexical sociocultural hypothesis testing. v2 evaluates contextual phenomena including AAVE, Yiddish/Hebrew usage and dance-related identity, with explicitly identity-related scenarios such as Judaism and Personal Cultural Identity.

E2.justification: The GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o theory-model comparison, together with Llama/GPT classifier comparisons, disappears. v2 instead compares five lexicon-generation prompts and evaluates Triviality filtering against an unfiltered baseline (Table 2; Figures 4 and 10). These replace the earlier comparison methods.

E3.justification: Topic retrieval changes from 3,000 posts per demographic/topic with a bottom-25% cutoff to up to 100,000 with LLM-guided filtering; the reported curated corpus changes from 3.6 million posts across 200 topics to 9.7 million across 89. Evaluation replaces 42-post calibration and three-post attribution sets with 781 corpus indices, a 2,000-post minimum and lift@0.5%. Human validation changes from model-selected cases with 0–4 ratings to 500 randomly sampled significant hypotheses with 1–5 ratings.

E4.justification: v1's calibration-size and classifier-choice sensitivity experiments and weak-model stereotype case analysis are removed. v2 adds analyses of prompt context and creativity, Triviality thresholds, demographic intersectionality, and whether the dataset captures known contextual linguistic phenomena (Sections 3.3 and 5–6; Appendices A–B).

E5.justification: v1 reports point results and explicitly avoids overlapping human ratings. v2 introduces one-tailed hypergeometric tests, significance reporting, 95% intervals for the random lift baseline in Figures 11–13, and three ratings per hypothesis with ICC(2,k) agreement and correlation significance. Neither version documents repeated seeded model runs.

E6.justification: v1's GPT-3.5 Turbo/GPT-4o mini/GPT-4o accuracies of 59.6/63.0/65.4% and appendix GT results are removed. v2 adds lexical findings, such as 3.16% versus 2.00% AAVE usage for Black versus non-Black Hip-Hop posts (Table 1). Table 2 reports filtering precision increasing from 0.270 to 0.480 at the 0.1 cutoff, with recall 0.178. These are new-task results, not comparable GT performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's formal GT generation/evaluation maps and custom human-scoring definitions are removed. v2 formalizes lexicon-conditioned PSLPs and defines Triviality through Rsubspace(L, demographic lexicon), while Appendix A.2 introduces the relevance-ranking assumption underlying cutoff search. The group-ness definition and self-identification assumptions remain; the change concerns formal task and scoring definitions rather than new theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace claims about benchmarking demographic social inference and stronger models producing better theories with contributions to systematic sociocultural discovery. v2 claims dataset validation through known phenomena, scalable lexical hypothesis evaluation, and a human-validated filter reducing inspections per promising finding by approximately 1.5–1.8 times.

C2.justification: v1's explanations involving calibration overfitting, classifier strength and weak-model demographic misrepresentation disappear. v2 interprets lexical patterns as preliminary sociocultural hypotheses and explicitly cautions that they are not established facts. It adds substantive limitations concerning lexical representation, platform-specific discourse, intersectionality, manual demographic lexica and LLM-generated topic bias, beyond the retained selection and temporal caveats.

D1.justification: v2 documents the cutoff model gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14, window size 100, target relevance 0.8 and tolerance 0.03, plus BERT embeddings, demographic lexica and five generation prompts. It adds pseudonymous-user-ID and MIT-license information. However, v1's explicit code/data URL and temperature-zero disclosure disappear, and v2 leaves the hypothesis-generation model unspecified.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from LLM cultural alignment and social-bias benchmarking to sociolinguistics, perspectivism, lexicon construction and automated discovery. v2 substantially expands these connections, including Geng et al., Havaldar et al. and Ishibashi et al., while removing much of v1's alignment-oriented literature. Several demographic-attribution dataset references remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, evaluation narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction now precedes the evaluation framework, the appendices are reorganized around the new study, and expanded ethics material accompanies a separate Limitations section. This is a substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. The GT diagram, accuracy plots and benchmark tables are replaced by a retrieval pipeline, lift–Triviality scatterplot, filtering and case-study displays, and additional heatmaps. The seed bubble plot and self-identification curves are retained but resized or relocated; dataset tables move into the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 better substantiates the dataset's scientific utility through known-phenomenon replications and randomly sampled human validation with three ratings per hypothesis and measured agreement, improving on v1's model-selected, nonoverlapping annotation study. Its explicit lexical and intersectional limitations also improve interpretability. These gains are tempered by missing generator/access details and Section 6's significance claims extending to p-values of 0.075. Table 2 supports reduced inspections per promising finding, but with substantial recall tradeoffs, limiting the strength of the overall improvement.
